introduction: These readings hold that the material and the spiritual act on each other: a melody made of vibrating air moves the spirit, a building of stone affects those who enter it, the body's health helps or hinders the soul, and friends parted by oceans remain together. The passages set beside them come from other scriptures and from poets and philosophers who noticed the same traffic in both directions, among them David's harp, Jacob's ladder, Paul absent in the flesh and present in the spirit, Plato and Shakespeare on music. Others pull the two apart or warn against leaning on outward things: Paul on flesh against spirit, Jeremiah and Kabir on temples, the gulf fixed in the parable of Lazarus. They are there to test how far the connection reaches.
questions: The readings begin with music. When has a sound, a place or an object changed your inward state, and what do you make of that?
Jeremiah and Kabir warn against trusting in a holy building. What keeps a material means of devotion from becoming a substitute for it?
Paul speaks of flesh and spirit as contrary; these readings speak of them as correlated. In your own life, when are body and spirit allies and when at odds?
James asks what use kind words are to someone who is hungry. What follows for how material and spiritual help should be offered together?
Several readings say that distance has no place in the world of the spirit, and Constance still feels her child's absence in every room. How do you hold both?

outside.why: Paul asks the Ephesians to speak to themselves in psalms and hymns, making melody in their heart to the Lord.
Plato held that rhythm and harmony find their way into the inward places of the soul and fasten mightily upon it.
When David took a harp and played, Saul was refreshed and was well, and the evil spirit departed from him.
Shakespeare's Lorenzo says that the man who is not moved by concord of sweet sounds is fit for treasons and not to be trusted.
Proverbs says that a merry heart does good like a medicine, and a broken spirit dries the bones.
Wordsworth tells of an eye made quiet by the power of harmony, with which we see into the life of things.
Elisha asked for a minstrel, and when the minstrel played the hand of the Lord came upon him.
Lorenzo says that such harmony is in immortal souls, but that while this muddy vesture of decay closes it in we cannot hear it. Does the body carry music to the spirit, or stand in its way?
Through Amos God refuses the songs and the melody of viols of people who neglect justice. What makes music heavenly: its sound, or the life of those who make it?
Paul says that whatsoever a man soweth, that shall he also reap.
Paul says that we have this treasure in earthen vessels, so that the power may be seen to be of God.
Jacob woke from his dream and said of an ordinary place: this is none other but the house of God, and this is the gate of heaven.
Kabir has God say: I am neither in temple nor in mosque; I am beside thee. What does a building add to what is already near?
The psalmist says that his soul longs and even faints for the courts of the Lord, and his heart and flesh cry out.
Jeremiah warns people not to trust in the words: the temple of the Lord, the temple of the Lord. When does trust in a holy building become a lying word?
Acts tells that handkerchiefs and aprons were carried from Paul's body to the sick, and their diseases departed.
The Book of Kings tells of a dead man who revived when his body touched the bones of Elisha.
Joshua set up twelve stones from the Jordan so that children would ask in time to come: what mean ye by these stones?
The Letter to the Hebrews says that the tabernacle was made after a pattern shown on the mount, a shadow of heavenly things.
The Lord's Prayer asks that God's will be done in earth, as it is in heaven.
Paul says that the invisible things of God are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made.
The Letter to the Hebrews says that things which are seen were not made of things which do appear.
Paul says that the things which are seen are temporal, but the things which are not seen are eternal.
Elisha prayed that his servant's eyes be opened, and the young man saw the mountain full of horses and chariots of fire.
The first letter to Timothy says that every creature of God is good, and nothing to be refused if received with thanksgiving.
Paul wrote to the Galatians that the flesh lusteth against the Spirit, and the two are contrary to one another. Are body and spirit partners or opponents, and what decides which?
The Preacher finds it good and comely to eat and drink and enjoy the good of one's labour, for it is one's portion.
Milton's angel tells Adam of a creation in which body works up to spirit, each thing in bounds proportioned to its kind.
Jesus told Nicodemus that what is born of the flesh is flesh, and what is born of the Spirit is spirit.
Genesis says that God formed man of the dust of the ground and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life.
Paul says that to be carnally minded is death, but to be spiritually minded is life and peace.
The Book of Job says that if God gathered to Himself His spirit and His breath, all flesh would perish together.
Juvenal advised people to pray for a sound mind in a sound body.
Mark tells of a woman who touched a garment in faith and felt in her body that she was healed.
Hamlet calls man noble in reason and like an angel in action, and then asks what this quintessence of dust is to him. How do the two descriptions belong to one creature?
Jeremiah felt the word he tried to hold back as a burning fire shut up in his bones.
Paul asks: know ye not that your body is the temple of the Holy Ghost which is in you?
Richard Lovelace wrote from confinement that stone walls do not a prison make, nor iron bars a cage.
Jesus said: render unto Caesar the things which are Caesar's, and unto God the things that are God's.
James Madison wrote that if men were angels no government would be necessary. Why does a spiritual order still need a political one beside it?
James asks what it profits to say to the hungry: be ye warmed and filled, and not give them what the body needs. When must material help come before spiritual words?
Marcus Aurelius told himself on waking unwillingly: I am rising to the work of a human being.
Jacob dreamed of a ladder set up on the earth whose top reached to heaven, with angels ascending and descending on it.
Isaiah says that the fast God has chosen is to share bread with the hungry and bring the poor into one's house.
The psalmist says that man has been made a little lower than the angels and crowned with glory and honour.
The second letter of Peter says that one day is with the Lord as a thousand years, and a thousand years as one day.
The psalm says that a thousand years in God's sight are but as yesterday when it is past.
In the parable of the rich man and Lazarus, Abraham says that a great gulf is fixed between the two sides, so that none can pass. Is the border between the worlds a gulf or a link?
The Preacher says that all are of the dust and all turn to dust again, and asks who knows whether the spirit of man goes upward. What grounds are there for calling the other world vast and near?
The psalm promises that God shall give His angels charge over thee, to keep thee in all thy ways.
The Letter to the Hebrews pictures the living as runners compassed about with a great cloud of witnesses.
The Qur’an says that on the Night of Power the angels and the Spirit descend, and it is peace until the rising of the dawn.
Paul says that if our earthly house were dissolved, we have a building of God not made with hands.
In Gethsemane Jesus told his sleeping disciples that the spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak.
Paul wrote to the Colossians: though I be absent in the flesh, yet am I with you in the spirit.
Paul told the Thessalonians that he had been taken from them in presence, not in heart.
Donne told the one he was leaving that their two souls endure not a breach but an expansion, like gold beaten thin.
Shakespeare's Constance says that grief fills the room of her absent child, lies in his bed and walks up and down with her. Does nearness of heart take away the body's missing of someone?
Jesus said that where two or three are gathered together in his name, he is in the midst of them.
Paul says that there is a natural body and there is a spiritual body.

The Qur’an says that God does not change the condition of a people until they change what is in their hearts. Which is to be reformed first, the heart or the surroundings, or can neither wait for the other?

samuel-david-took-an-harp.text: And it came to pass, when the evil spirit from God was upon Saul, that David took an harp, and played with his hand: so Saul was refreshed, and was well, and the evil spirit departed from him

kings-when-the-minstrel-played.text: But now bring me a minstrel. And it came to pass, when the minstrel played, that the hand of the Lord came upon him

acts-handkerchiefs-or-aprons.text: And God wrought special miracles by the hands of Paul: So that from his body were brought unto the sick handkerchiefs or aprons, and the diseases departed from them, and the evil spirits went out of them

matthew-in-earth-as-in-heaven.text: Thy kingdom come, Thy will be done in earth, as it is in heaven

ephesians-melody-in-your-heart.text: Speaking to yourselves in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing and making melody in your heart to the Lord

joshua-what-mean-these-stones.text: That this may be a sign among you, that when your children ask their fathers in time to come, saying, What mean ye by these stones? Then ye shall answer them, That the waters of Jordan were cut off before the ark of the covenant of the Lord; when it passed over Jordan, the waters of Jordan were cut off: and these stones shall be for a memorial unto the children of Israel for ever

hebrews-shadow-of-heavenly-things.text: Who serve unto the example and shadow of heavenly things, as Moses was admonished of God when he was about to make the tabernacle: for, See, saith he, that thou make all things according to the pattern shewed to thee in the mount

kings-bones-of-elisha.text: And it came to pass, as they were burying a man, that, behold, they spied a band of men; and they cast the man into the sepulchre of Elisha: and when the man was let down, and touched the bones of Elisha, he revived, and stood up on his feet

galatians-flesh-lusteth-against-spirit.text: For the flesh lusteth against the Spirit, and the Spirit against the flesh: and these are contrary the one to the other: so that ye cannot do the things that ye would

timothy-every-creature-of-god-is-good.text: For every creature of God is good, and nothing to be refused, if it be received with thanksgiving
